quests.instruction: Choose the three statements that together cover the story without repeating each other, and put them in order.
quests.story: Pia's team needed a venue for a workshop for forty people. She phoned three community halls and visited two of them, then chose the one with a projector and step-free access. She paid the deposit the same day and emailed the participants the address on Monday.
options: Pia chose the hall with a projector and step-free access and paid the deposit the same day.
Pia phoned three community halls and visited two of them.
Pia visited two of the community halls in person before choosing.
Pia emailed the participants the address on Monday.
quests.hint: If one option is only a piece of another, using both means repeating yourself.
quests.explanation: Visiting two halls is already part of the first combined statement, so it adds a repeat and leaves the second half of that idea missing. The whole story is covered by the search, the choice and deposit, and the email.
storyKeyEvents: Pia phoned three community halls and visited two of them.
Pia chose the hall with a projector and step-free access and paid the deposit the same day.
Pia emailed the participants the address on Monday.

quests.instruction: Each correct statement combines related events. Choose the three that cover the whole story, in order.
quests.story: Kaveh's application for a design job needed a CV and a portfolio. He updated his CV on Tuesday and spent Wednesday choosing six projects for the portfolio. On Thursday he wrote a cover letter and sent everything in one email. The company replied on Friday and invited him to an interview.
options: Kaveh wrote a cover letter and sent the whole application in one email on Thursday.
The company replied on Friday and invited him to an interview.
Kaveh wrote his cover letter and was invited to an interview on Thursday.
Kaveh updated his CV and chose six projects for his portfolio.
quests.hint: When you combine two events, they must have happened together in the story.
quests.explanation: The cover letter was written on Thursday, but the invitation came from the company on Friday. Joining them merges two separate days and two separate people's actions.
storyKeyEvents: Kaveh updated his CV and chose six projects for his portfolio.
Kaveh wrote a cover letter and sent the whole application in one email on Thursday.
The company replied on Friday and invited him to an interview.

quests.instruction: Choose the three statements that give a complete, non-repeating summary.
quests.story: Deborah's car failed its annual test because of worn brake pads and a blown headlight bulb. The garage replaced both the same afternoon, and Deborah collected the car at five. She then booked the retest for the next morning, and it passed.
options: The garage replaced the parts the same afternoon because the test centre insisted.
Deborah's car failed its annual test because of worn brake pads and a blown headlight bulb.
The garage replaced both parts that afternoon and Deborah collected the car at five.
Deborah booked the retest for the next morning and the car passed.
quests.hint: A merged statement should only add reasons that the story supplies.
quests.explanation: No reason for the same-day repair is given, and the invented "insisted" is not in the story. The accurate merge keeps the replacement and collection together without extra causes.
storyKeyEvents: Deborah's car failed its annual test because of worn brake pads and a blown headlight bulb.
The garage replaced both parts that afternoon and Deborah collected the car at five.
Deborah booked the retest for the next morning and the car passed.

quests.instruction: Choose the three statements that together cover the story without repeating each other, and put them in order.
quests.story: Mr. Abara organised a charity walk around the lake. He marked the route with yellow arrows on Friday evening and hung banners at the start line. On Saturday two hundred walkers set off at nine, and the last of them finished by one. That evening the committee counted the donations and posted the total online.
options: The committee posted the total online before it had counted the donations.
That evening the committee counted the donations and posted the total online.
Mr. Abara marked the route with yellow arrows and hung banners on Friday evening.
Two hundred walkers set off at nine on Saturday and the last finished by one.
quests.hint: Check the order inside a combined statement as well as between statements.
quests.explanation: The committee first counted and then posted the total. Reversing them inside one statement changes what happened.
storyKeyEvents: Mr. Abara marked the route with yellow arrows and hung banners on Friday evening.
Two hundred walkers set off at nine on Saturday and the last finished by one.
That evening the committee counted the donations and posted the total online.

quests.instruction: Each correct statement combines related events. Choose the three that cover the whole story, in order.
quests.story: The town library's old computers had been slow for years. In March the library received a grant, bought twelve new computers, and moved the old ones to a storeroom. Staff spent a week training visitors to use the new machines, and by April the queue for computers had disappeared.
options: Staff spent a week training visitors to use the new machines.
By April the queue for computers had disappeared.
The library received a grant, bought twelve new computers, and stored the old ones.
The library's old computers had been slow for many years.
quests.hint: Ask whether an option describes something that happened or how things were before.
quests.explanation: The slowness is background that came before the story's events and is not one of the changes. The three statements that cover what happened are the purchase, the training, and the vanished queue.
storyKeyEvents: The library received a grant, bought twelve new computers, and stored the old ones.
Staff spent a week training visitors to use the new machines.
By April the queue for computers had disappeared.

quests.instruction: Choose the three statements that give a complete, non-repeating summary.
quests.story: Two colleagues, Neve and Otis, arranged the office move. Neve booked the removal firm and ordered the packing crates, while Otis measured the new floor and planned the desk layout. On Friday the removal firm moved the furniture, and on Monday everyone worked from the new office.
options: Neve booked the removal firm and ordered the packing crates.
Otis measured the new floor and planned the desk layout.
The firm moved the furniture on Friday and everyone worked from the new office on Monday.
Neve booked the removal firm and planned the desk layout.
quests.hint: Combine tasks only when the same person did them.
quests.explanation: Neve's jobs were the firm and the crates, and the desk layout was Otis's. Mixing the two gives Neve a task that belonged to her colleague.
storyKeyEvents: Neve booked the removal firm and ordered the packing crates.
Otis measured the new floor and planned the desk layout.
The firm moved the furniture on Friday and everyone worked from the new office on Monday.

quests.instruction: Choose the three statements that together cover the story without repeating each other, and put them in order.
quests.story: Ravindra recorded the first episode of his podcast on a Saturday. He tested three microphones, chose the one that picked up the least background noise, and set up his desk near the quietest wall. After recording forty minutes of conversation with his guest, he edited out the pauses and uploaded the episode on Sunday night.
options: Ravindra got all of his equipment ready and then made the episode.
Ravindra recorded forty minutes of conversation with his guest.
Ravindra edited out the pauses and uploaded the episode on Sunday night.
Ravindra tested three microphones, chose the quietest, and set up his desk near the quietest wall.
quests.hint: A summary can be short and still be too vague to tell you what happened.
quests.explanation: The vague statement compresses so much that it hides the microphone testing, the recording and the editing. A useful merge keeps enough detail to say what was actually done.
storyKeyEvents: Ravindra tested three microphones, chose the quietest, and set up his desk near the quietest wall.
Ravindra recorded forty minutes of conversation with his guest.
Ravindra edited out the pauses and uploaded the episode on Sunday night.

quests.instruction: Each correct statement combines related events. Choose the three that cover the whole story, in order.
quests.story: The volunteers at the animal shelter cleaned the kennels and washed the blankets on Saturday morning. Because two dogs were due to go to new homes, they also brushed the dogs and updated the adoption files. The shelter's vet visited at noon. In the afternoon the new owners collected both dogs.
options: The new owners collected both dogs in the afternoon.
The volunteers cleaned the kennels, washed the blankets, and reorganised the storeroom.
The volunteers cleaned the kennels and washed the blankets on Saturday morning.
They brushed the two dogs due to go to new homes and updated the adoption files.
quests.hint: Everything in a merged statement should come from the story.
quests.explanation: The storeroom is never mentioned, so it adds an event the volunteers didn't do. The first accurate combination stops at the kennels and blankets.
storyKeyEvents: The volunteers cleaned the kennels and washed the blankets on Saturday morning.
They brushed the two dogs due to go to new homes and updated the adoption files.
The new owners collected both dogs in the afternoon.

quests.instruction: Choose the three statements that give a complete, non-repeating summary.
quests.story: Zsofia's ceiling started leaking after heavy rain. She put a bucket underneath and reported it to the landlord, who sent a roofer that week. The roofer found broken tiles, replaced them, and sealed the edges. The next storm passed without a drop coming through.
options: Zsofia's ceiling leaked after heavy rain, so she put a bucket underneath and reported it.
The landlord's roofer found broken tiles, replaced them, and sealed the edges.
The roofer fixed the leak on the same day it began.
The next storm passed without a leak.
quests.hint: Merging can hide a gap in time. How long did the story say it took?
quests.explanation: The landlord sent the roofer later that week, after Zsofia's report. Saying the fix happened the same day squeezes out the waiting time.
storyKeyEvents: Zsofia's ceiling leaked after heavy rain, so she put a bucket underneath and reported it.
The landlord's roofer found broken tiles, replaced them, and sealed the edges.
The next storm passed without a leak.

quests.instruction: Choose the three statements that together cover the story without repeating each other, and put them in order.
quests.story: The volunteers' litter-pick in the park started with four people, but two of them arrived late because of a bus delay. The organiser split the park into four zones and gave the latecomers the smallest ones. All four zones were finished by noon.
options: The litter-pick started with four volunteers, two of whom arrived late because of a bus delay.
All four zones were finished by noon.
All four volunteers arrived late because of a bus delay.
The organiser split the park into four zones and gave the latecomers the smallest ones.
quests.hint: Count how many people the story says were late.
quests.explanation: Only two of the four volunteers were delayed, so saying all four arrived late overcounts them. The story runs from the start with two latecomers, to the zones, to the finish by noon.
storyKeyEvents: The litter-pick started with four volunteers, two of whom arrived late because of a bus delay.
The organiser split the park into four zones and gave the latecomers the smallest ones.
All four zones were finished by noon.

quests.instruction: Each correct statement combines related events. Choose the three that cover the whole story, in order.
quests.story: For the school trip to the science museum, Ms. Lund collected permission slips from twenty-six of the twenty-eight pupils and phoned the parents of the last two. She booked the coach for eight o'clock and asked two parents to help supervise. The trip went ahead, and the pupils returned to school by four.
options: The trip went ahead and the pupils were back at school by four.
Ms. Lund collected permission slips from twenty-six pupils and phoned the parents of the last two.
Ms. Lund booked the coach for eight and asked two parents to help supervise.
Ms. Lund phoned the parents of the last two pupils about the permission slips.
quests.hint: A statement that repeats only half of another one is redundant.
quests.explanation: The phone calls are already included in the first statement, so choosing them again repeats it while losing the permission slips. The three combined statements cover the whole trip.
storyKeyEvents: Ms. Lund collected permission slips from twenty-six pupils and phoned the parents of the last two.
Ms. Lund booked the coach for eight and asked two parents to help supervise.
The trip went ahead and the pupils were back at school by four.

quests.instruction: Choose the three statements that give a complete, non-repeating summary.
quests.story: The bookshop's summer sale started with a window display of discounted paperbacks. Anouk relabelled four hundred books with red stickers and rearranged the tables by price. On the first day a queue formed at opening, and the shop sold half its paperbacks by closing time.
options: Anouk relabelled four hundred books and rearranged the tables by price.
Anouk relabelled four hundred books and then sold half of them at opening time.
A queue formed at opening and half the paperbacks had sold by closing time.
The bookshop began its summer sale with a window display of discounted paperbacks.
quests.hint: Merge events only if the story links them.
quests.explanation: Anouk's relabelling and the day's sales were done at different times, and the sales weren't hers alone. The statement forces two separate events together.
storyKeyEvents: The bookshop began its summer sale with a window display of discounted paperbacks.
Anouk relabelled four hundred books and rearranged the tables by price.
A queue formed at opening and half the paperbacks had sold by closing time.

quests.instruction: Choose the three statements that together cover the story without repeating each other, and put them in order.
quests.story: Emil's new business website went live in June. He had spent May writing the product descriptions and photographing thirty items. In the first month the site received about nine hundred visitors, and forty of them bought something.
options: Emil spent May writing product descriptions and photographing thirty items.
In the first month about nine hundred people visited and forty bought something.
Emil's website went live in June.
Emil's website went live in June because a competitor had launched a similar site.
quests.hint: A reason should be in the text, not just believable.
quests.explanation: No competitor is mentioned; the preparation in May is the only stated reason the site was ready. The unsupported "because" changes the story.
storyKeyEvents: Emil spent May writing product descriptions and photographing thirty items.
Emil's website went live in June.
In the first month about nine hundred people visited and forty bought something.

quests.instruction: Each correct statement combines related events. Choose the three that cover the whole story, in order.
quests.story: Lisbeth's language exam had two parts. On Thursday she took the written paper and the listening test. On Friday she had a spoken interview with two examiners. Results came by email three weeks later, and she passed with a distinction in speaking.
options: Three weeks later an email said she had passed with a distinction in speaking.
On Thursday Lisbeth took the written paper and the listening test.
Lisbeth had her spoken interview before the written paper and the listening test.
On Friday Lisbeth had a spoken interview with two examiners.
quests.hint: Check the order inside each option against the days named.
quests.explanation: The written and listening parts were on Thursday and the interview came on Friday. Reversing them contradicts the days.
storyKeyEvents: On Thursday Lisbeth took the written paper and the listening test.
On Friday Lisbeth had a spoken interview with two examiners.
Three weeks later an email said she had passed with a distinction in speaking.

quests.instruction: Choose the three statements that give a complete, non-repeating summary.
quests.story: The village hall's gutter had been a problem for years, and every autumn the drain overflowed. This October the committee hired a roofer, who cleared the gutter and fitted a new downpipe in one afternoon. The following week's storm left the hall dry.
options: The following week's storm left the hall dry.
The roofer cleared the gutter and fitted a new downpipe in one afternoon.
The committee hired a roofer this October.
The drain had overflowed every autumn for years.
quests.hint: Ask whether an option describes the story's actions, or its history.
quests.explanation: The yearly overflow is the situation before the story's actions. What happened runs from hiring the roofer, to the repair, to the dry hall.
storyKeyEvents: The committee hired a roofer this October.
The roofer cleared the gutter and fitted a new downpipe in one afternoon.
The following week's storm left the hall dry.

quests.instruction: Choose the three statements that together cover the story without repeating each other, and put them in order.
quests.story: Two siblings, Dara and Femi, cleared their late uncle's garage. Dara sorted the tools into keep and donate piles, while Femi took the broken furniture to the tip. Together they swept the floor and locked the garage.
options: Dara sorted the tools into keep and donate piles.
Dara sorted the tools and took the broken furniture to the tip herself.
Together they swept the floor and locked the garage.
Femi took the broken furniture to the tip.
quests.hint: One person can't be credited with both siblings' jobs.
quests.explanation: The tip run was Femi's task, so merging it into Dara's leaves her with two jobs. Each sibling's separate job and their shared finish make the correct three.
storyKeyEvents: Dara sorted the tools into keep and donate piles.
Femi took the broken furniture to the tip.
Together they swept the floor and locked the garage.

quests.instruction: Each correct statement combines related events. Choose the three that cover the whole story, in order.
quests.story: Chiara's team recruited a summer intern. They advertised the role on two job sites and shortlisted four candidates from thirty applications. They interviewed the four over a video call, and they offered the job to Lena, who accepted the same day.
options: The team advertised the role on two job sites and shortlisted four candidates from thirty applications.
The team handled all the hiring and eventually found someone for the job.
The team interviewed the four candidates over a video call.
The team offered the job to Lena, who accepted the same day.
quests.hint: A merged statement must still say what was actually done.
quests.explanation: The vague sentence hides the advertising, the shortlist and the video interviews. It compresses without showing the steps that lead to Lena.
storyKeyEvents: The team advertised the role on two job sites and shortlisted four candidates from thirty applications.
The team interviewed the four candidates over a video call.
The team offered the job to Lena, who accepted the same day.

quests.instruction: Choose the three statements that give a complete, non-repeating summary.
quests.story: Baptiste's morning run took him along the river to the old mill and back. He stopped twice to stretch. At the mill his time was three minutes better than the previous week. He finished in forty-two minutes and logged the run in his app.
options: Baptiste stopped twice to stretch on the way to the mill.
At the mill his time was three minutes better than the previous week.
Baptiste ran along the river to the old mill.
Baptiste finished in forty-two minutes and logged the run in his app.
quests.hint: Some true details don't belong in a compressed summary.
quests.explanation: The two stretch stops are accurate but they don't change the run's story. The summary needs the route, the improved time at the mill, and the finish and log.
storyKeyEvents: Baptiste ran along the river to the old mill.
At the mill his time was three minutes better than the previous week.
Baptiste finished in forty-two minutes and logged the run in his app.

quests.instruction: Choose the three statements that together cover the story without repeating each other, and put them in order.
quests.story: Nadir's team submitted a grant application on the last day of the deadline. They had written the budget on Monday and had the narrative proof-read on Tuesday. After a month the funder asked for two clarifications, and the team answered both within a day. The grant was awarded in April.
options: The grant was awarded straight after the application was submitted.
The grant was awarded in April.
The funder asked for two clarifications, and the team answered both within a day.
Nadir's team wrote the budget, had the narrative proof-read, and submitted on the last day.
quests.hint: Check the time gaps in the story before joining two events.
quests.explanation: A month passed between the submission and the funder's questions, and the award came later still. Placing the award straight after the submission removes those gaps.
storyKeyEvents: Nadir's team wrote the budget, had the narrative proof-read, and submitted on the last day.
The funder asked for two clarifications, and the team answered both within a day.
The grant was awarded in April.

quests.instruction: Each correct statement combines related events. Choose the three that cover the whole story, in order.
quests.story: Sunita trained for a sponsored swim over three evenings. She swam twelve lengths on the first, eighteen on the second and twenty-four on the third. At the event she completed forty lengths, which raised £180 from her sponsors.
options: At the event Sunita completed forty lengths.
Over three evenings Sunita built up from twelve to twenty-four lengths.
Her sponsors gave £180.
Sunita swam twelve lengths on each of the three evenings.
quests.hint: Look at how many times a number applies.
quests.explanation: The lengths increased each evening, from twelve to twenty-four. The statement repeats the first number for all three evenings.
storyKeyEvents: Over three evenings Sunita built up from twelve to twenty-four lengths.
At the event Sunita completed forty lengths.
Her sponsors gave £180.

quests.instruction: Choose the three statements that give a complete, non-repeating summary.
quests.story: The council resurfaced Church Lane over two weekends. On the first, crews scraped off the old asphalt and fixed the drains. On the second, they laid the new surface and painted the lines. Traffic returned on Monday morning, and residents said the street was much quieter.
options: Traffic returned on Monday and residents found the street quieter.
Crews fixed the drains on the first weekend of the resurfacing.
Crews laid the new surface and painted the lines on the second weekend.
Crews scraped off the old asphalt and fixed the drains on the first weekend.
quests.hint: If two options overlap, keep the one that covers more.
quests.explanation: Fixing the drains is already part of the first combined statement, so using it again repeats and also drops the scraping. Together the three combined statements cover both weekends and the result.
storyKeyEvents: Crews scraped off the old asphalt and fixed the drains on the first weekend.
Crews laid the new surface and painted the lines on the second weekend.
Traffic returned on Monday and residents found the street quieter.

quests.instruction: Choose the three statements that together cover the story without repeating each other, and put them in order.
quests.story: Waleed arranged a surprise for his colleague's retirement. He collected signatures for a card from forty staff and ordered a small engraved clock. On the last day he and two teammates presented both gifts at the tea break, and the colleague read the card aloud.
options: Waleed collected signatures on the clock and engraved the card at the tea break.
Waleed collected forty signatures for a card and ordered an engraved clock.
The colleague read the card aloud.
Waleed and two teammates presented the card and the clock at the tea break.
quests.hint: Objects and actions must be matched correctly when events are combined.
quests.explanation: The signatures belong on the card and the engraving on the clock, and neither took place at the tea break. The statement swaps objects and moves the preparation into the presentation.
storyKeyEvents: Waleed collected forty signatures for a card and ordered an engraved clock.
Waleed and two teammates presented the card and the clock at the tea break.
The colleague read the card aloud.

quests.instruction: Each correct statement combines related events. Choose the three that cover the whole story, in order.
quests.story: Ottilie moved to a new city for work. She rented a flat near the station on the first weekend and joined a running club in the second week. After a month she knew four neighbours by name and no longer felt like a newcomer.
options: Ottilie rented a flat near the station on the first weekend and joined a running club in the second week.
Ottilie joined the running club because her landlord recommended it.
Ottilie moved to a new city for work.
After a month she knew four neighbours by name and felt at home.
quests.hint: Ask where the story states the reason for the action.
quests.explanation: No reason for joining the club is given, and the landlord isn't mentioned. The merge of flat and club stays accurate by leaving out the invented cause.
storyKeyEvents: Ottilie moved to a new city for work.
Ottilie rented a flat near the station on the first weekend and joined a running club in the second week.
After a month she knew four neighbours by name and felt at home.

quests.instruction: Choose the three statements that give a complete, non-repeating summary.
quests.story: Mrs. Yilmaz's book club runs a simple cycle. In January the members chose a short novel. In February they met to discuss it at the library, and in March they voted for a longer book for spring.
options: In March they voted for a longer book for spring.
In February they met at the library to discuss it.
The members discussed the short novel before they had chosen it.
In January the members chose a short novel.
quests.hint: The months give you a timeline. Does each option respect it?
quests.explanation: The novel was chosen in January and discussed in February. A discussion before the choice would reverse the cycle.
storyKeyEvents: In January the members chose a short novel.
In February they met at the library to discuss it.
In March they voted for a longer book for spring.

quests.instruction: Choose the three statements that together cover the story without repeating each other, and put them in order.
quests.story: Marek had wanted to learn the guitar for years. In September he bought a second-hand guitar and signed up for weekly lessons. By December he could play three songs, and at his sister's birthday he played one of them for the family.
options: Marek bought a second-hand guitar and signed up for weekly lessons in September.
At his sister's birthday he played one of them for the family.
Marek had wanted to learn the guitar for years.
By December Marek could play three songs.
quests.hint: Something that was true before the story starts isn't one of its events.
quests.explanation: The long-held wish is the reason behind the story but not something that happened in it. The events are the purchase and lessons, the three songs, and the birthday performance.
storyKeyEvents: Marek bought a second-hand guitar and signed up for weekly lessons in September.
By December Marek could play three songs.
At his sister's birthday he played one of them for the family.

quests.instruction: Each correct statement combines related events. Choose the three that cover the whole story, in order.
quests.story: In the office kitchen, Peter refilled the coffee machine and cleaned the milk fridge, while Alma restocked the tea shelf and wiped the counters. Then the two of them wrote a rota on the whiteboard so everyone would share the jobs.
options: Peter refilled the coffee machine and cleaned the milk fridge.
Alma restocked the tea shelf and wiped the counters.
Together they wrote a rota on the whiteboard so everyone would share the jobs.
Peter refilled the coffee machine and wiped the counters.
quests.hint: Check each job against the person who did it.
quests.explanation: Wiping the counters was Alma's task, so it cannot be merged into Peter's. Each person's two jobs stay together in the correct statements.
storyKeyEvents: Peter refilled the coffee machine and cleaned the milk fridge.
Alma restocked the tea shelf and wiped the counters.
Together they wrote a rota on the whiteboard so everyone would share the jobs.

quests.instruction: Choose the three statements that give a complete, non-repeating summary.
quests.story: Tavita's flat viewing was a disappointment. The kitchen was damp, the bedroom window would not close, and the agent could not say when they would be repaired. Tavita asked the agent to send a written list of repairs with dates, and the agent emailed it two days later. Tavita decided to look at other flats.
options: Tavita asked for a written list of repairs with dates and received it two days later.
The viewing went badly and Tavita moved on.
The flat had a damp kitchen and a bedroom window that would not close, with no repair dates.
Tavita decided to look at other flats.
quests.hint: A short summary should still keep the step that connects the start to the end.
quests.explanation: The vague version skips Tavita's request and the emailed list, which is what leads to her decision. The correct three cover the problem, the request and reply, and the choice.
storyKeyEvents: The flat had a damp kitchen and a bedroom window that would not close, with no repair dates.
Tavita asked for a written list of repairs with dates and received it two days later.
Tavita decided to look at other flats.

quests.instruction: Choose the three statements that together cover the story without repeating each other, and put them in order.
quests.story: Ferran reorganised the shop's storeroom over a weekend. He labelled every shelf by product category and moved the heavy boxes to the bottom shelves. He also threw out two bins of expired stock. His radio played all weekend. On Monday the staff found items in half the usual time.
options: Ferran listened to his radio all weekend while he worked.
On Monday the staff found items in half the usual time.
Ferran threw out two bins of expired stock.
Ferran labelled every shelf by category and moved the heavy boxes to the bottom shelves.
quests.hint: Ask whether the detail helps explain why the storeroom worked better.
quests.explanation: The radio was on, but it played no part in the reorganisation or its result. The story is the labelling and moving, the clear-out, and the faster finding.
storyKeyEvents: Ferran labelled every shelf by category and moved the heavy boxes to the bottom shelves.
Ferran threw out two bins of expired stock.
On Monday the staff found items in half the usual time.

quests.instruction: Each correct statement combines related events. Choose the three that cover the whole story, in order.
quests.story: The city's cycle-hire scheme launched with two hundred bikes. Within a week forty had been vandalised or stolen, so the operator fitted stronger locks and a tracker to every bike. Over the next two months losses fell to three.
options: The cycle-hire scheme launched with two hundred bikes.
Over the next two months losses fell to three.
Within a week forty bikes had been vandalised or stolen, so the operator fitted stronger locks and trackers.
Losses fell to three as soon as the locks were fitted.
quests.hint: Look at how long the story says the improvement took.
quests.explanation: The fall in losses took two months, not an instant. The statement shrinks the timeline and hides that the effect built up gradually.
storyKeyEvents: The cycle-hire scheme launched with two hundred bikes.
Within a week forty bikes had been vandalised or stolen, so the operator fitted stronger locks and trackers.
Over the next two months losses fell to three.

quests.instruction: Choose the three statements that give a complete, non-repeating summary.
quests.story: The hospital's outpatient clinic tried a new appointment system. For the first two weeks patients waited about forty minutes on average. After staff added a text reminder, the average fell to twenty-five minutes over the next three weeks. After five weeks the clinic made the reminder permanent.
options: After text reminders were added, the average wait fell to twenty-five minutes over three weeks.
For the first three weeks patients waited about forty minutes on average.
After five weeks the clinic made the reminders permanent.
For the first two weeks patients waited about forty minutes on average.
quests.hint: Check how many weeks each stage lasted.
quests.explanation: The forty-minute waits lasted two weeks; the next three weeks were the improved ones. Stretching the first stage to three weeks miscounts the timeline.
storyKeyEvents: For the first two weeks patients waited about forty minutes on average.
After text reminders were added, the average wait fell to twenty-five minutes over three weeks.
After five weeks the clinic made the reminders permanent.
